title: GreenLine transit project breaks ground after a decade of debate
summary: The GreenLine transit project began construction this week after ten years of planning and contentious public review. Officials called the milestone a turning point for regional mobility, while residents along the route gave mixed reviews citing both expected commute benefits and concerns about years of disruption.

sentiment.rationale: Evaluative language appears on both sides with comparable weight ('turning point', 'years of disruption'). Signal is genuinely weak; analyzer enforced confidence-clamp rule, so label is held to neutral and score bounded into [-0.2, 0.2].

key_claims.claim: Construction of the GreenLine transit project has begun.
Officials described the groundbreaking as a turning point for regional transportation.
Some residents praised the expected commute-time improvements.
Other residents expressed concerns about construction noise, dust, and street closures.
Construction is expected to last roughly four years.
The project is funded through federal grants and a 2024 transit bond.
